title: Introduce harmonic emit coordinator with KV synergy and graded backpressure
author: Evan Brooks
description: Context: We observed persistent streaming first-byte tail latency for medium-length responses (tokens 8..128) caused by misaligned emitter ticks, inefficient microbatching at low emission density, and cold KV lookups triggered just-in-time. This PR introduces a coordinated emitter layer (the "harmonic emit coordinator") that aligns emission ticks to kernel execution windows, applies graded per-stream backpressure using harmonic credit shaping, and plugs in an anticipatory KV prefetcher that uses short-horizon sequence hints to warm the KV cache before kernel execution. The combined change targets stable TTFB improvements without sacrificing peak throughput. What changed (high-level): - New coordination layer: runtime/emitter/harmonic_coordinator.rs implements a lightweight tick harmonizer that observes kernel run windows and schedules flushes on harmonic boundaries to reduce interleaved kernel churn. - Graded backpressure: emitter now applies a per-stream harmonic credit curve (fast-path for hot streams, gentle damping for cold streams) to avoid sudden flushes that cause kernel scatter. - KV synergy: runtime/kv/prefetcher.rs introduces a predictive prefetch hook; when a stream's emission density and token context match a learned warmup pattern, we probe the KV cache early and bias kernel placement to nodes with warmer caches. - Continuous microcoalescer: runtime/batcher/continuous.rs coalesces sub-token microbatches within a short adaptive window when pending emissions are sparse; avoids draining immediate credits to preserve kernel affinity. - Kernel policy: runtime/scheduler/kernel_policy.rs updated to consider emission_density and kv_warmth_score when selecting execution kernels and packing microbatches. - Tests and docs: added integration tests and a performance explainer in docs/perf/emit-coordinator.md. Rollout plan: Canary at 5% traffic in the US region, metric gates on median TTFB, p95/p99, and overall token/s GPU efficiency; automatic rollback if p99 regresses > 8% during canary. Observed outcomes in internal benchmarks: - Median TTFB reduction: 12% - p95 reduction: 22% - p99 reduction: 35% on medium-length responses under mixed workload in our perf lab - End-to-end throughput unchanged within noise (+/-2%) on dense generation workloads; slight throughput dip (~2%) in extreme microburst scenarios but with much lower tail latency tradeoff. Backwards compatibility: behavior is feature-flagged as "harmonic_emit" and off by default for Dedicated/Private until customer opt-in. Compatibility with model variants: kernel selection fallbacks remain in place; if KV hints are unavailable, coordinator degenerates to conservative flush cadence. Related: builds on ideas from earlier credit/granularity PRs but rethinks scheduling from a coordinator-first perspective. This description includes the motivation, design, and rollout plan in one continuous narrative.
